learning_outcomes.description: Describe physiological mechanisms that support the functions of the major organ systems in the human body.
Explain how nervous and endocrine signals are essential to whole-body physiological responses.
Identify normal physiological responses and distinguish them from abnormal responses associated with human disease.
Investigate how the human body responds to challenges and attempts to maintain homeostasis.
Perform key observational and experimental techniques in human physiology, including acquisition and analysis of quantitative data.
Design and implement a physiological experiment, and critically analyse and communicate its findings, with supporting evidence from the scientific literature.
Reflect on your learning and skill development in scientific methods and communication
Work and learn collaboratively, capitalising on the diverse abilities, backgrounds and perspectives within the group

An introduction to BIOM2012 Systems Physiology. Course overview including learning activities and assessment.

learning_activities.topic:
Autonomic Nervous System [Anderson]

Students will work through an online module covering fundamental aspects of the Autonomic Nervous System. Sympathetic and Parasympathetic division. Flight or fight response. Autonomic ganglia, and pre- versus post-ganglionic fibres. Sympathetic variscosities - smooth muscle innervation. Cholinergic and adrenergic transmission and control of internal organs and homeostasis.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

learning_activities.topic:
Cardiovascular System [Anderson]

A 6 lecture series on the Cardiovascular System. Physiology of the circulation, including blood flow, vascular function, capillary fluid exchange, lymphatics, venous return, and the pulmonary circuit. Regulation of cardiac output and mean arterial pressure, including baroreceptor and chemoreceptor reflexes, long-term regulation of blood pressure, and pathophysiology of hypertension.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

learning_activities.topic:
Neuromotor System [Noakes]

A 5 lecture series on the Neuromotor System. Physiology of the neuromotor system which will include the following: the effector organ of the neuromotor system skeletal muscle; how muscle action potentials are generated via the neuromuscular synapse; neuromuscular diseases; the basis of graded muscle contraction; ageing neuromotor system; sensory - sensing and controlling body position and movement; alpha and gamma motor neurons - spinal cord organisation; motor neuron circuits revealed by reflexes; roles of brain and brain stem motor centres in the control of movement - posture, voluntary movement and correction of ongoing movement.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

learning_activities.topic:
Renal System [Rajapaske]

A four lecture module on the renal system. Renal physiology and regulation, including glomerular filtration through the nephron's three-layered filtration barrier, maintenance of water and electrolyte balance, intrinsic myogenic mechanisms and tubuloglomerular feedback regulating glomerular filtration rate, assessment of renal function using creatinine clearance, and urine concentration through the countercurrent multiplier system with hormonal regulation by antidiuretic hormone and aldosterone.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

A 5 Lecture series on the Respiratory System. Physiology of the respiratory system, including respiratory mechanics (inspiration and expiration, quiet and forced breathing), factors affecting ventilation (including respiratory membrane, airway/alveolar factors), gas exchange, gas transport (oxygen and carbon dioxide), and control of respiration.

A four lecture series on the Gastrointestinal System. Digestion and absorption processes in the GIT. Phases of gastric secretion. Digestive enzymes and functions. Motility in the GIT and the enteric nervous system. Liver anatomy and structure, functions of the liver, and the circadian clock.

Endocrinology [Anderson]

A 6 lecture series on metabolic physiology.  Glucose homeostasis and key roles of insulin & glucagon. Diabetes Mellitus - type 1, type 2 and gestational diabetes. Insulin insensitivity. Cortisol, stress and metabolism. Growth Hormone and metabolism. Exercise & energy metabolism. Energy balance and the control of appetite.

learning_activities.topic:
Muscle Fatigue [Launikonis]

A 2 lecture on muscle physiology, relating to muscle fatigue. Muscle fatigue is a reversible exercise-induced reduction in the ability of a muscle (or muscle group) to generate force or power, whether or not the task can still be continued. In these lectures the different types of muscle fatigue will be presented, with a focus on the the intracellular components that cause this.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

learning_activities.topic:
Integrated Physiology [Anderson]

This final, integrative systems physiology lecture explores how the body balances fed and fasted states by regulating energy storage (anabolism) and release (catabolism), including important biochemical processes such as gluconeogenesis and ketogenesis via hormonal control.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
